{{Top}} {{Otheruses|Bib}} {{Update|[[Han Solo & Chewbacca 5]], [[Han Solo & Chewbacca 10]], [[The Hoojib Menace]], [[Star Wars (2020) 10]], [[Star Wars (2020) 11]], [[War of the Bounty Hunters – Jabba the Hutt 1]], [[Bounty Hunters 11]], [[Bounty Hunters 12]], [[Star Wars (2020) 14]], [[Bounty Hunters 14]], [[War of the Bounty Hunters 5]], [[Star Wars (2020) 39]], [[Tales from the Rancor Pit]], [[Galactic Tales: Valnir and Laizhu]], [[Return of the Jedi – Jabba's Palace 1]], [[Chapter 1: Stranger in a Strange Land]], [[Chapter 3: The Streets of Mos Espa]], [[Chapter 4: The Gathering Storm]], [[Disney Gallery: The Mandalorian: Making of Season Two]], [[Star Wars Insider 206]], [[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Bounty Hunters]]}} {{Character |type=Criminal |image=[[File:BibFortuna-CEUEEd.png]] |option1=9 ABY |image2=[[File:BibFortuna-SWE.png]] |option2=4 ABY |image3=[[File:Wood_Fortuna_closeup.png]] |option3=32 BBY |name=Bib Fortuna |homeworld=[[Ryloth]]''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' |birth= |death=[[9 ABY]],{{InsiderCite|202|A Certain Point of View}} dates the [[Second rescue of Grogu]] to "9 ASW4" or [[9 ABY|nine years after]] the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars: ''Episode IV'' A New Hope'']], including the [[Battle of Yavin]]. {{InsiderCite|211|A Certain Point of View}} similarly dates the [[Assassination attempt on Boba Fett]] to 9 ABY. Since the epilogue of "[[Chapter 16: The Rescue]]" takes place between the second rescue of Grogu and the assassination attempt on [[Boba Fett]], it can be concluded that the events of the epilogue, including Bib Fortuna's death, occurred in that same [[Standard year|year]]. [[Tatooine]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}} |species=[[Twi'lek]]{{Databank|bib-fortuna|Bib Fortuna}} |gender=[[Gender|Male]] |pronouns=He/him |height=2 [[meter]]s |mass= |hair= |feathers= |eyes=[[Color|Red]][[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (paperback novel)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]] |skin=Pale |cyber= |families=[[Fortuna family]]''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' |parents= |partners= |siblings= |children= |affiliation=*[[Hutt Clan]]{{Film|VI}} **[[Jabba's criminal empire]] |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|Jabba the Hutt is dead, long live Jabba the Hutt. His empire is now ripe for the taking, and I, for one, know just the person to lead it to greatness.|Bib Fortuna|{{StoryCite|story=Fortuna Favors the Bold|book=From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi}}}} '''Bib Fortuna''' was a [[Twi'lek]] [[Gender|male]] who lived on the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. He served as [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]'s [[majordomo]] and chief of staff for [[Standard decade|decades]], handling all of the day-to-day operations at [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]], while secretly hating the Hutt and longing for a chance to [[Death|kill]] him in order to assume his place. By [[32 BBY]], Fortuna had assumed the position as Jabba's majordomo, and it was he and the [[Hutt]] who oversaw that year's [[Boonta Eve Classic]], in which a nine-year-old [[Anakin Skywalker]] won the podrace. By the time of the [[Proclamation of the New Order|formation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], Fortuna continued to serve Jabba as his right-hand-man. In [[19 BBY]], Fortuna contacted [[Ciddarin Scaleback|Cid]] and asked that she retrieve a [[rancor]], [[Muchi]], from [[Zygerrian]] [[enslaver]]s. With the help of [[Clone Force 99]], Murchi was brought to Fortuna, who in turn brought the rancor to Jabba. Twenty-three years later, and Fortuna continued to serve Jabba. That year, [[Luke Skywalker]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] went to Tatooine to rescue [[Han Solo]]. During a battle over the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]], Jabba was [[Death|killed]] by [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] and his sail barge, [[Khetanna]], was destroyed. Following Jabba's death, Fortuna assumed control of his palace as a [[crime lord]], becoming obese in the process. In [[9 ABY]], Fortuna was killed by [[bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett]], who took over his [[Fett gotra|throne]]. ==Biography== ===Early years=== {{Quote|What a pleasant surprise. I'm graced by the presence of Jabba's right-hand man.|Cid|{{TBB|Rampage (episode)}}}} [[File:Jabba_Boonta_Eve.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Bib Fortuna came to serve Jabba the Hutt]] A [[Gender|male]] [[Twi'lek]], Bib Fortuna hailed from [[Ryloth]], the [[homeworld]] of his [[species]]. Fortuna was [[Reproduction|born]] to a [[Fortuna family|prominent clan]] that had close ties to the criminal underworld, though his more politically minded cousin [[Beezer Fortuna|Beezer]] resented his family's associations. Before coming into the service of [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], Fortuna worked as a [[Slavery|slave]] trader, one who was focused on members of his own species. He became rich from selling his fellow Twi'leks into slavery.''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' At some point, Fortuna came into Jabba's service and competed against [[Bidlo Kwerve]] to become the Hutt's [[majordomo]].[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] Fortuna also gave Jabba his pet [[rancor]]''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' [[Pateesa]]''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]'' as a [[birthday]] present. Ultimately, Fortuna succeeded and claimed the job whereas Kwerve ended up as an early victim of the rancor. In truth, however, Fortuna hated Jabba and longed to find a chance to [[Death|kill]] him, hoping to claim [[Jabba's criminal empire]] for himself. [[File:Bib_TPM.png|thumb|right|250px|Fortuna attends the Boonta Eve Classic.]] He served as Jabba's majordomo as far back as the [[time]] of the [[Invasion of Naboo]],{{Film|I}} in [[32 BBY]].''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' That [[Standard year|year]], Fortuna attended the [[Boonta Eve Classic]], which his master hosted to commemorate the [[Boonta Eve]] holiday.{{Databank|boonta-eve-classic-podracer-pilots|Boonta Eve Classic Podracer Pilots}} From his master's private balcony, he witnessed the victory of a local [[human]] boy named [[Anakin Skywalker]] against the reigning champion [[Sebulba]]. As the Hutt was not interested in podracing aside from the [[gambling]] aspect of the sport, Jabba fell asleep before the end of the race, forcing Fortuna to wake him up in order to announce the ending. ===Imperial Era=== ====The Ord Mantell ordeal==== {{Quote|Assure your employer he'll be reunited with Muchi soon.|Cid, to Bib Fortuna|}} [[File:Bib-and-Cid.png|thumb|left|270px|Tired of her promises, Bib Fortuna personally journeyed to Cid's office for an update on the rescue of Muchi.]] As the years of [[Timeline of galactic history|galactic history]] passed, Fortuna continued to serve Jabba as the [[Galactic Republic]] was reorganized into the [[Galactic Empire]].{{Film|III}} In [[19 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' places the events of [[The Bad Batch Season 1|''The Bad Batch'' Season 1]] in [[19 BBY]]. during the early [[Standard day|days]] of the [[Imperial Era]], Fortuna came into contact with [[Ciddarin Scaleback|Cid]], a [[Trandoshan]] who operated on the planet [[Ord Mantell]], and hired her to [[Mission to Ord Mantell (Clone Force 99)|retrieve]] the young [[rancor]] [[Muchi]] from a group of [[Zygerrian]] [[enslaver]]s. As [[time]] passed and Muchi was not yet rescued, however, Fortuna contacted her via [[hologram]], informing her that Jabba was impatient and wanted to know why the rancor had not yet been returned.{{TBB|Rampage (episode)}} {{AD|Disney+}} As she ate, Cid noted that the operation required a delay due to planning and asked him to assure Jabba that Muchi would soon be rescued. Although Fortuna attempted to threaten her, Cid remained unintimidated, claiming she had her best team working to save the rancor. Cid had actually hired [[Clone Force 99]], a group of [[clone commando]] deserters she had only just met and who she was uncertain could actually succeed. With Muchi still not returned to Jabba, Fortuna arrived personally at [[Cid's Parlor]] with two [[Gamorrean Warrior]]s, entering into her office and demanding an update on behalf of Jabba. Cid again claimed Muchi would be rescued, trying to ease his concerns after he threatened consequences for failure by noting how delicate the operation was. Before Fortuna could respond to her request that Jabba be patient, Muchi was heard outside, as Clone Force 99 had succeeded in their mission. Quickly getting outside to reunite with Muchi, the majordomo was overjoyed to see his master's pet safe, greeting the young rancor before ordering a guard to give Cid her payment with a snap. With the rancor safe, Fortuna told her they would return home before leaving with his guards. Cid proceeded to give Clone Force 99 thirty percent of Fortuna's payment, as they had agreed upon. ====Solo troubles==== {{Quote|''«Marshal Buck Vancto''. To what do I owe the pleasure? And by 'pleasure,' I, of course, mean having my afternoon ''interrupted''.''»
"''I'm pursuing a ''warrant'' out for Han Solo. I'm given reason to believe he's doing a job for your slug as we speak.|quotestart=0|Bib Fortuna and Buck Vancto|[[Han Solo & Chewbacca 2|''Han Solo & Chewbacca'' 2]]}} Later in the Imperial Era, Jabba welcomed two new [[smuggler]]s into his employ, the [[Corellian]] human [[Han Solo]] and his [[Wookiee]] [[Pilot|co-pilot]] [[Chewbacca]]. As the Hutt's majordomo, Fortuna often found himself dealing with the pair, handing them assignments from Jabba and delineating their pay. One such assignment[[Han Solo & Chewbacca 1|''Han Solo & Chewbacca'' 1]] between around [[8 BBY]] and [[2 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Star Wars: Han Solo & Chewbacca]]'' to between around [[8 BBY]] and [[2 BBY]]. was no different, as Fortuna informed Solo that the Hutt [[lord]] was willing to pay one million [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] for the delivery of a [[verillix]] [[Unidentified urn|urn]] that contained the ashes of [[Krestrel D'Naran]], a rival of Jabba. To Solo's dismay, Fortuna also specified that the smugglers would be required to work with [[Greedo]], a [[Rodian]] [[bounty hunter]] of Jabba's who had been the first to learn of the urn. Reluctantly, the trio agreed to the [[Heist on Corellia|job]] and headed for Solo's homeworld of [[Corellia]]. With some personal time to spare, Fortuna gallivanted to the streets of [[Mos Espa]] to bet on [[nuna]] fights, where he promptly lost one thousand of his own credits. During his time off, Fortuna was questioned by an old acquaintance, [[Buck Vancto]] of the [[Benelex Marshal Service]], who was pursuing a warrant put out on Solo for a recent [[heist on Galator III]]. Knowing that the Twi'lek owed him a favor, Vancto threatened to drag Fortuna back to Ryloth should he not disclose Solo's location. Although Fortuna took the [[marshal]]'s warning seriously, he feared retribution from Jabba, and agreed to divulge the information so long as Vancto waited to apprehend Solo until after the smuggler had completed his mission. ===Galactic Civil War=== ====Conflicts on Tatooine==== {{Quote|Those men worked for my master, the mighty Jabba the Hutt. He is most displeased with your hostility.|Bib Fortuna contacts the mercenaries following the battle|''[[Star Wars: Commander]]''}} During the [[Galactic Civil War]] between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]], the Twi'lek remained in Jabba's service. A short time after the [[Battle of Yavin]], which had cost the Empire its [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|DS-1 Death Star Mobile Battle Station]], the Empire elected to open negotiations with Jabba, but a [[Heroes of Yavin|Rebel strike team]] took advantage of the negotiations to [[Assault on Cymoon|destroy]] [[Weapons Factory Alpha]]. Following that loss, the Empire moved negotiations to take place at Jabba's Palace, but the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth]] Vader arrived a day early to request bounty hunters for private business. After Vader arrived and [[Death|killed]] two [[Gamorrean]] warriors, Fortuna ran to the [[Sith]] to speak with him, only to be met with a [[Darth Vader's lightsaber|lightsaber]] and a demand to see Jabba. Rushing to his master, Fortuna awoke him and informed him of what had happened. Fortuna stood beside Jabba as he began to talk with Vader, who ordered him to remove the audience so they could talk in private. After Jabba had many of them return in a failed attempt to collect the [[bounty]] on Vader's head, the Sith Lord threatened him with a [[Force choke]], and the Hutt crime lord acquiesced, having his two best bounty hunters—[[Boba Fett]] and [[Krrsantan]]—dispatched to fulfill Vader's missions.[[Darth Vader (2015) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 1]] The following day, Vader returned to oversee the Empire's official negotiations, accompanied by [[stormtrooper]]s. Although Fortuna tried to greet Vader, the Sith Lord cut off his pleasantries, beginning the ultimately successful negotiations with Jabba.[[Star Wars (2015) 4|''Star Wars'' (2015) 4]] At some point between the Battle of [[Yavin]] and [[Battle of Hoth]], Fortuna contacted the Tatooinian [[mercenary]] [[Saponza]] and [[Saponza's partner|his partner]] in the name of Jabba. The two men had reacted violently to the presence of Jabba's henchmen around [[Saponza's homestead]], killing six of them. Fortuna let the two mercenaries know they had made an enemy of his Hutt master. Some time later, Jabba's henchmen razed Saponza's estate to the ground in retaliation, and the majordomo contacted Saponza once again to gloat over his misfortune and warn him that Jabba's revenge was not over. ====Return of Crimson Dawn==== {{Quote|All of you want to live. Who doesn't? But I promise. Fight me…some of you die. Maybe ''most'' of you. And you'd be dying…for ''him''. Doesn't seem fair, does it?|Boba Fett convinces Jabba's court not to lay their lives down for Bib Fortuna|[[War of the Bounty Hunters 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters'' 1]]}} In [[3 ABY]], Boba Fett [[Escape from Cloud City|captured]] Han Solo, who had since fallen out of Jabba's favor and earned a price on his head from the mighty Hutt. En route to the crime lord's [[Boba Fett's Palace|Tatooinian palace]] with his [[bounty]], Fett contacted Fortuna and assured the majordomo that Solo was alive, safely secured within [[Carbon-freezing|frozen]] [[carbonite]]. To Fortuna's confusion, however, Fett abruptly ended their communication when the [[carbonite matrix]] containing Solo became unstable, forcing him to take a detour to [[Nar Shaddaa]] to fix the issue. There, Solo was stolen from Fett[[War of the Bounty Hunters Alpha 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters Alpha'' 1]] by agents of [[Crimson Dawn]], a [[The galaxy|galactic]] crime syndicate that had long been considered obsolete. Fett declined to immediately inform Fortuna of his bad luck, instead simply telling the Twi'lek that his delivery would "be a [[Standard minute|minute]]." Representing the interests of an increasingly impatient Jabba, Fortuna warned Fett not to disappoint the mighty Hutt lord. Soon after, Crimson Dawn sent invitations to many of the major crime lords in the galaxy, including Jabba. Revealing that they held Solo in their possession, they bid the invitees to travel to [[Jekara]] and witness the return of Crimson Dawn. Believing that Fett had cheated him and sold the smuggler to a competitor, Jabba placed a bounty on the [[Hunting|hunter's]] head before departing for Jekara, leaving Fortuna to look over his palace. Unaware that the Hutt had left, Fett stormed through the castle's dusty gates, incinerating two Gamorrean guards and demanding that Fortuna give him answers. After explaining that his master was absent, Fortuna suggested that Fett leave, lest the retinue of thugs and mercenaries that made up Jabba's court turn their weapons on the hunter. Fett reminded the rabble, however, that many of their number would perish in a firefight against him, dying in the meager name of Bib Fortuna. With this in mind, no one fired a shot. At the behest of Fett, Fortuna showed him Jabba's invitation, which depicted a [[Qi'ra|human woman]] requesting that her audience "await the Dawn." Accepting her as his new target, Fett ordered Fortuna to have his ship, ''[[Slave I]]'', repaired of damage it had sustained on Nar Shaddaa before leaving for Jekara himself. Fett was eventually successful in his mission, managing to retrieve the frozen Han Solo and deliver him to Jabba intact. At some point before or during [[4 ABY]],{{SW|url=news/the-illustrious-jabba-the-hutt-bids-you-welcome-to-his-new-marvel-comic-jabbas-palace-exclusive-reveal|text=The Illustrious Jabba the Hutt Bids You Welcome to His New Marvel Comic, ''Jabba's Palace'' - Exclusive Reveal}} establishes that [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (2023)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'']], including [[Return of the Jedi – The Rebellion 1|''Return of the Jedi – The Rebellion'' 1]], takes place in the era of {{Film|VI}}, which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[4 ABY]]. As ''Return of the Jedi – The Rebellion'' 1 establishes that Zarah Bliss had [[Death|died]] prior to the events of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]], she must have died by 4 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]]. Fortuna helped ensure that [[Zeva Bliss]] could arise to power over the [[Spice Runners of Kijimi]], further ensuring that her mother and its current leader, [[Zarah Bliss]], fell from power,[[Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising 2|''Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising'' 2]] with Zarah ultimately dying.[[Return of the Jedi – The Rebellion 1|''Return of the Jedi – The Rebellion'' 1]] ====Trouble at the Great Pit of Carkoon==== =====Enter the Rebellion===== {{Quote|Die wanna wanga!|Bib Fortuna|}} [[File:BibFortunaJabba-CGSWG.png|thumb|right|250px|Fortuna serving alongside Jabba at the palace during the Galactic Civil War.]] Later in the war, Fortuna greeted two [[droid]] visitors to his master's palace. The two mechanical units, called [[C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2]], claimed that they had a gift for the Hutt. The majordomo demanded that they hand over that gift to him so he could bring it to Jabba himself, but the droids answered that their instructions were to give it only to the crime lord himself. Fortuna relented, and led the droids into the throne room, where they delivered a [[Hologram|holographic message]] from their owner, the Rebel hero and fledgling [[Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker]]. In the message, Skywalker asked to bargain for the life of his friend Han Solo, offering C-3PO and R2-D2 in exchange. Fortuna was present when [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] arrived under the disguise of notorious bounty hunter [[Boushh]]. She brought along a chained Chewbacca and demanded a higher payment for the Wookiee's capture, under the threat of a [[thermal detonator]]. Later that night, Fortuna was hiding alongside Jabba as part of the Hutt's plan to capture Organa when she attempted to free Solo herself. Jabba had Solo sent to the dungeons, while Organa was enslaved. =====Mind-tricked majordomo===== {{Quote|He's no Jedi.|Bib Fortuna, to Jabba the Hutt, regarding Luke Skywalker|}} The next morning Luke Skywalker [[Rescue of Han Solo|arrived]] to rescue his friends. Fortuna tried to stop him from entering the audience chamber. However, he was influenced by Skywalker's [[mind trick]], though he was not as weak-minded as some of Jabba's other guards. Skywalker only succeeded in his mind trick by finding and exploiting Fortuna's weak point,''[[Return of the Jedi: Beware the Power of the Dark Side!]]'' his alleged strong loyalty to Jabba. Fortuna proceeded to wake Jabba, and presented the Jedi to his master. Angry that Fortuna had been manipulated by Skywalker, Jabba pushed him off his dais. As the negotiations became more tense, Jabba dropped Skywalker into the rancor pit. After the Jedi slew the beast, he was imprisoned and sentenced to death, with Jabba wanting him executed at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]]. =====Making preparations===== Before the visit to Carkoon, Fortuna prepped [[Klatooine paddy frogs]] in a larder in the palace. One of the creatures escaped containment, causing Fortuna to decide an excruciating death for the paddy frog, though the Twi'lek's thoughts were interrupted by a delivery droid beeping at him. After deciphering the beeps, Fortuna ordered the droid to put the paddy frog pallet in the middle of the larder. As the droid left, Fortuna thought about calling the droid back and getting the pallet delivered to its correct location but did not like the thought of communicating with the droid without C-3PO, who was already aboard Jabba's [[sail barge]], the ''[[Khetanna]]''. Fortuna briefly thought about turning his hidden blaster on the droid but restrained himself as his blaster was a one-shot weapon, and he hated enacting vengeance on immaterial annoyances. As a rumbling laughter shook the walls of the palace, the Twi'lek took a step backwards, accidentally killing the paddy frog. As Jabba's laughter continued, Fortuna instinctively reached for the blaster in his cloak. Taking a deep breath and relaxing, he removed the blaster from his clothing and stuck the pistol to a wall—with sticky paddy-frog residue—behind a stack of beverage tanks where no one would see it. Using a datapad, the Twi'lek instructed for the tanks to be loaded onto the ''Khetanna''. Clenching a fist as the Hutt continued to laugh, Fortuna had the plan of murdering his master that day. To the majordomo's annoyance, the delivery droid returned, this time with more paddy-frogs. The Twi'lek sighed and wondered if there was a second blaster he could use. Now in the palace's hanger bay, as one of Jabba's skiff's needed fixing, Fortuna was of half a mind to blow the vehicle up. His thoughts went to Jabba, who he was lost in a fantasy about killing, until a Gamorrean went up to him for a question. The alien communicated that that there would be eight guards on the skiff holding the prisoners. After Fortuna told the Gamorrean that only seven guards were necessary, the alien continued that he'd heard Jabba wanted to be there during the execution. Realizing that one more guard on the sail barge was one more in the way of him getting to kill Jabba, Fortuna let the Gamorrean keep the guard on the skiff. The majordomo then told the Gamorrean to leave and close the door on the way out, which he did punching the door controls, making Fortuna give a snarl of frustration that could be heard from throughout the palace. =====Execution time===== Fortuna accompanied Jabba and many of his palace denizens to the pit. One the way over, Jabba pulled Organa over to him, telling her she will soon learn to appreciate him as Fortuna pushed her to him. As the ''Khetanna'' arrived at its destination, Fortuna looked out a window to view the proceedings, before moving to sit in the sail barge's kitchen. As he thought about leaving Jabba's service and realized that Jabba would kill him as he knew too much, Max Rebo entered for keys to his instrument. He told the Ortolan that he really should get back to the topside of the sail barge to check in on the serving droids, and that he would string the droid manager up if one of his charges went rouge. The rebels managed to escape custody, kill Jabba, and destroy his sail barge. Though he was presumed to have died in the explosion,{{HelmetCollectionCite|18|Databank A-Z}} Fortuna survived the battle.{{InsiderCite|219|Day Wanna Wanga - The Tale of the Twi'leks}} ===Death=== {{Quote|Boba. I thought you were dead. I am so glad to see you. I had heard many rumors.|translated=1|Bib Fortuna's final words|}} [[File:Bib_Fortuna_MS2-EP8.png|thumb|left|200px|Fortuna as a crime lord]] After Jabba's death, Fortuna gained control of Jabba's palace and amassed servants and slaves of his own, becoming a crime lord.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}} {{AD|Disney+}} Over time, he lived an unhealthy lifestyle consisting of over-indulgence and inactivity.''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' Years into Fortuna's reign,{{Topps|set=2023 Topps Star Wars|cardname=8D8|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/370777/cid/22170335}} after the [[second rescue of Grogu]], Boba Fett and his companion [[Fennec Shand]] [[Attack on Jabba's Palace (Boba Fett)|arrived]] at the palace, killing Fortuna's guards and releasing an [[Unidentified Rutian Twi'lek|enslaved individual]] of Fortuna's. The Twi'lek greeted Fett and said he believed the bounty hunter had died, and that he had heard many rumors regarding him. Fett immediately shot Fortuna, killing him and assuming Fortuna's throne in the palace. Following his death, Boba Fett visited the many vassals of Jabba the Hutt and Bib to continue the crime underworld on Tatooine. Unlike Bib Fortuna and Jabba, Boba intended to rule with respect, catching the eye of many.{{BOBF|Chapter 1: Stranger in a Strange Land}} According to Fennec Shand, Fortuna was a terrible leader with no right to the throne.{{BOBF|Chapter 4: The Gathering Storm}} ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Great Jabba… I regret to inform you… a Coruscant cartel figured out how to ''synthesize'' the desert wine… and n-now… it's… it's… worthless.''»
«''Worthless? No, fool… ''[drinks the desert wine]'' it was ''priceless''.|translated=1|Bib Fortuna and Jabba the Hutt|[[Age of Rebellion - Jabba the Hutt 1|''Age of Rebellion - Jabba the Hutt'' 1]]}} [[File:FortunaAgainstSandPeople-AORJabba1.png|thumb|right|250px|The majordomo of Jabba the Hutt, Bib Fortuna would greet all who arrived at his master's palace.]] A pasty-faced male Twi'lek who served Jabba the Hutt for decades despite secretly hating the Hutt, Fortuna greeted all those who sought an audience with the Hutt, forcing those who wanted to meet with Jabba to maneuver past the majordomo. Even so, Fortuna at times understood his duties included denying visitors permission to see Jabba, whom he called his master. The majordomo held great patience thanks to his job, needing to deal with individuals ranging from haughty emissaries to drunken ruffians. Even so, the Trandoshan Cid felt that Fortuna could get too impatient and nervous when an operation was taking a long time. Additionally, his master's own volatile mood was another possible job hazard, especially because Jabba did not have the same respect Fortuna showed towards him; Jabba believed Fortuna to be a fool. Indeed, the majordomo proved to be weak minded enough for Luke Skywalker to use a mind trick on him once Skywalker exploited his seeming loyalty to the Hutt. Otherwise, Fortuna was not as weak minded as some of Jabba's other guards. When not leaving Jabba's side to greet visitors or travel off-planet, Fortuna often remained at the side of his master, whispering advice and information. When talking, Fortuna elected to only speak [[Huttese]] despite understanding other languages and sometimes using words from [[Galactic Basic Standard]]. Fortuna was also willing to threaten business partners in order to try to get better results. Able to represent Jabba on off-world missions, a visit from the greatest ally of the Hutt was considered an honor, although Cid mocked Fortuna during one such occasion. Nevertheless, Fortuna cared greatly about Jabba's interests, being overjoyed when the rancor Muchi was rescued. Fortuna also cared greatly for Muchi, calling the rancor his "sweet girl." Following the minimal protocol rules that existed in Jabba's court and marking excessive concerns with propriety and modesty, Fortuna was mortified upon hearing Sy Snootles's saucy lyrics for the song ''[[Jedi Rocks]]''. Fortuna maintained a list of seven hundred and sixty-two items that he hated. At the top of the list was none other than Jabba, and Klatooine paddy frogs were also far up, although Fortuna was ultimately able to develop a taste for them. Item three hundred and five was wastefulness, and according to his recollection, maintenance requests were in the six hundreds. He also had no love for the bounty hunter Boba Fett, whom he thought of as a suck-up and a stumbling glory-hound. Max Rebo was at one point on his list, though the Ortolan found his way off due to his jatz-wail music capturing the tense feeling of working for a crime lord. Fortuna would have deeply loved to have used his "conversation starter" tools on Luke Skywalker, as he had, in the Twi'lek's mind, made a fool of him. Upon learning of Jabba's death, Fortuna laughed madly and decided to begin eating the paddy frogs he had previously hated, electing to cement himself as his own master by trying the second most hated item on his list. While he was a crime lord, Fortuna had grown larger in size and was scared of Fett, attempting to act friendly to the bounty hunter, only for his attempts to fail when Fett assassinated him. ==Equipment== During his servitude to Jabba, Fortuna wore a black-colored overcoat, black boots, and a chestplate.''[[Star Wars Costumes: The Original Trilogy]]'' In order to document his extensive list of things he hated, Fortuna, for redundancy's sake, used three datapads and the memory banks of a repurposed service droid. When executions were scheduled, the Twi'lek had favorited tools that he called "conversation starters," which he used to extract information from the people sent to death. After taking control of Jabba's palace[[Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising 2|''Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising'' 2]] in 4 ABY,The events of ''[[Star Wars: Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising]]'' take place after the [[Battle of Endor]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[4 ABY]]. The series is also set before the events of ''[[Star Wars: Battle of Jakku — Republic Under Siege]]'', which in turn are before the [[Liberation of Sullust]], an event dated to 4 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]] by ''Timelines''. Fortuna wore bandages on his head and lekku. By 9 ABY, he sat upon a throne and wielded a staff. ==Behind the scenes== ===Creation and costume=== {{Quote|He was one of my favorite characters. Phil started the design and I picked it up. I actually did a whole bunch of those Twi'lek creatures, because I wanted to populate them all over the place.|Nilo-Rodis Jamero|}} Bib Fortuna was played by [[Michael Carter]] and voiced uncredited by the late [[Erik Bauersfeld]], who also voiced [[Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar]], in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. In earlier drafts of ''Return of the Jedi'', Fortuna's title was the "High Beeser of [[Hoth]]," and his original design sketches depicted him as a wizened old human man sporting a dark cloak and a tall hat. References to this title and design, however, were left out from the finished version of the film.{{DB|character|bibfortuna|Fortuna, Bib}} The character's sharp fingernails and teeth were inspired by a [[Wikipedia:National Geographic|''National Geographic'']] article on the indigenous people of [[Wikipedia:Borneo|Borneo]], which to [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero|Nilo-Rodis Jamero]] was a favorite source of inspiration. The makeup process that Michael Carter needed to perform to create the custom of Bib Fortuna took over eight hours to first transform Carter into the Twi'lek advisor. By the end of Carter's five-week shoot, make-up artist [[Nick Dudman]] had streamlined the process down to 58 minutes. Removing the make-up took another 25 minutes. The most intricate effect was Fortuna's "air bladders" or bubbles. These were made of foam and latex that were fitted in Carter's brows and temples and inflated by off-stage-operated hoses to make them appear to pulsate. Carter also used dayglow orange contacts and claw-like finger extensions.{{SW|url=news/much-to-learn-you-still-have-7-things-you-might-not-know-about-twileks|text=Much to Learn You Still Have: 7 Things You Might Not Know About Twi'leks}} ===Later appearances=== Fortuna was portrayed by sound engineer [[Matthew Wood]] in{{DB|character|bibfortuna|Fortuna, Bib}} the podrace scene in the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film ''[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace]]'', who remained uncredited for the role. [[Alan Ruscoe]] also played a different visually similar Twi'lek character in the film. The character was one of the aides of [[Senator]] [[Orn Free Taa]] on [[Coruscant]] and was nicknamed "Bib Fortuna" by the production crew, but was ultimately cut from the final film. However, Ruscoe still described his character as Fortuna in an interview with [[Star Wars Insider 117|''Star Wars Insider'' 117]] in [[2010]]. Ruscoe was initially only contracted to portay [[Plo Koon]] in the film, but ended up also portraying [[Daultay Dofine]] and "Fortuna". He wore a major three piece prostetic that took four hours to apply and two additional hours to remove. In the interview, Ruscoe empathized that it was "nothing" compared to the time Carter needed for his makeup and that the real work was done by the makeup artists and not him.{{InsiderCite|117|Phantom Menaces (article)}} [[Kilian Plunkett]] created unused concept art of Bib Fortuna during the initial production of the animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' in July [[2006]].''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' Wood later reprised his role as Fortuna in a post-credits scene in "[[Chapter 16: The Rescue]]," the [[The Mandalorian Season Two|season two]] finale of ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' released in [[2020]], where he was subsequently killed. [[Jesse La Flair]] served as a stunt double in the episode. Wood again reprised his role in "[[Rampage (episode)|Rampage]]," the fifth episode of the [[The Bad Batch Season 1|first season]] of the animated series [[Star Wars: The Bad Batch]], released in [[2021]]. Fortuna's model for "Rampage" was completed by [[Angela Chen]] on [[August 8]], [[2019]].
